text:
support_tina: Heads up — large hosted API customer hitting a lot of 502/504s since ~09:12 UTC. They see timeouts on /v1/generate and spikes in gateway latency. Suspect prefix cache/memcached dependency; customer reports sudden error surge during billing cycle spike. Escalating.

sre_jordan: Can you paste the first error sample and any request IDs? Also which model + route?

support_tina: reqid=rid_0a9f4e, route=/v1/generate?model=gpt-large, timeframe 09:12–09:20 UTC. Snippet from gateway: `Upstream read timeout (110)`, and a bunch of 502s with "cache lookup failed" in gateway logs.

devops-bot: ALERT memcached-pfx-prod - OOMs detected on memcached-7 (10.4.2.11) 09:11:34 UTC - process restarted by systemd. Connection drops observed ~09:11:30–09:13:00.

maya: I rolled out a change to memcached slab config last night (reduce slab class to free memory) — reverted on staging but not prod. Rolling back now?

eng-ryan: Hold on before a hard rollback. Two parallel quick mitigations: 1) enable API fallback to origin cache-store (bypass memcached prefix) for the affected route, 2) increase gateway upstream timeout from 15s->30s to prevent immediate 502. Small config patch:
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "upstream_timeout_s": 30,
  "cache_fallback": "origin"
}
```

eli: Repro steps I ran from my laptop (inc logs):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
# response: 502 Bad Gateway after 12s, gateway logs: "prefix lookup error: connection reset by peer"
```

sre_jordan: Good repro. Forensics: memcached OOM leads to process restart -> connections reset -> many prefix lookups failing and gateway returning 502s. We should take memcached out of rotation and let gateway use origin KV fallback. Also check if prefix eviction raised thundering herd.

eng-ryan: Steps I'll do now: 1) mark memcached-7 as draining in service discovery, 2) push cache_fallback=true for /v1/generate (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%), 3) bump gateway timeout. Doing canary to avoid wide blast.

support_tina: I've notified the customer and logged the incident. They're seeing ~30% failed calls in that window, revenue-impacting. They asked for ETA.

maya: Initiating drain: `sdctl set-drain memcached-7 --cluster=prefix-prod` — done. Also increasing memcached memory_limit on memcached-8 as temporary.

devops-bot: TASK memcached-7 drained; traffic redirected. memcached-8 memory_limit bumped +10%.

sre_jordan: Monitoring: gateway 502 rate dropped from 28% -> 6% in 3 minutes. Latency p95 improved from 2.4s -> 1.1s. Continue to watch for cache miss storm.

eng-ryan: After canary completes will re-evaluate slab config and implement safety throttle to avoid sudden eviction storms. Also recommend adding auto-fallback rule: if memcached node restarts >3 times in 10m then auto-disable prefix cache for affected route.

eli: Adding sample logs from gateway for incident window:
```
[09:12:03] gw: upstream read timeout (110) reqid=rid_0a9f4e route=/v1/generate conn=184
[09:12:04] gw: prefix lookup error: unexpected EOF host=memcached-7:11211
[09:12:07] gw: returning 502 to client reqid=rid_0a9f4e
```

support_tina: Customer replied — thanks for the quick mitigation, asked for RCA and timeline for full fix. I'll prepare a post-incident runbook.

sre_jordan: RCA notes for runbook: cause = memcached slab tuning change + traffic spike during billing cycle -> evictions and OOM -> memcached restart -> prefix cache lookups fail -> gateway immediate 502s. Mitigations: drain failing nodes, enable origin fallback, increase upstream timeout, add restart/auto-disable safety.

eng-ryan: I'll open a follow-up PR for auto-fallback rule and a runbook checklist for on-call. tagging @eng-oncall for review.

support_tina: Closing loop — customer will hold on further escalations until RCA doc. I'll attach timeline and metrics once we have them. :thumbsup:
